lessons.title: Mean as equal sharing
lessons.label: Mean as equal sharing
lessons.objective: Explain the mean as an equal share of the same total.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Changing the total while finding the average.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must the total stay {{total|words}} while we redistribute?

steps.title: Different groups, same kind of counter
steps.explanation: The groups contain {{low|words}}, {{mean|words}} and {{high|words}} counters. There are {{total|words}} counters altogether.

$if.then: Move one from the largest group
Move one more to make equal groups
Move one counter from the group of {{high|words}} to the group of {{low|words}}. The total stays {{total|words}}.
Move one more counter from the largest group to the smallest. Now every group has {{mean|words}}.
$if.else: Move one more counter from the largest group to the smallest. The total stays {{total|words}}.

$if.then: One counter moved. The groups now contain {{small|words}}, {{mean|words}} and {{large|words}}.
A {{n|ordinal}} counter moved. Each of the three groups now has {{mean|words}}.
$if.else: Another counter moved. The groups now contain {{small|words}}, {{mean|words}} and {{large|words}}.

steps.title: The mean is the equal share
steps.explanation: {{total|Words}} counters shared equally between three groups gives a mean of {{mean|words}}.

scene.description: The total is still {{total|words}} and every group has {{mean|words}}.

lessons.title: Find the median
lessons.label: Find the median
lessons.objective: Order a data set and locate its middle value.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Choosing the middle value in the unsorted list.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we sort the values before choosing the middle?

steps.title: Read the five values
steps.explanation: The median is the middle value after the data is put in order.

scene.description: Values {{d|words}}, {{a|words}}, {{e|words}}, {{b|words}} and {{c|words}} in their original order.

steps.title: Put the same values in ascending order
steps.explanation: Rearrange the cards from smallest to largest. No value is added or removed.

scene.description: The same cards sorted as {{a|words}}, {{b|words}}, {{c|words}}, {{d|words}} and {{e|words}}.

steps.title: Pair the outside values
steps.explanation: Set aside the smallest and largest together. Three values remain between them.

scene.description: The outside values {{a|words}} and {{e|words}} are crossed out.

steps.title: Find the middle value
steps.explanation: Pair {{b|words}} with {{d|words}}. {{c|Words}} is left in the middle, with two values on each side.

scene.description: {{c|Words}} is selected in the middle. Two values lie on each side.

constraints.message: Keep the five median ranks in strict ascending order.

lessons.title: Find the mode
lessons.label: Find the mode
lessons.objective: Find the value that occurs most frequently.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Reporting how many times a value occurs instead of the value itself.

$if.then: Which value occurs most often, and how many times does it occur?
$if.else: Why is the mode {{mode|words}} rather than three?

steps.title: Read the values
steps.explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most often.

steps.title: Group equal values together
steps.explanation: Rearrange the same cards so repeated values sit together.

scene.description: The same values sorted as {{low|words}}, {{mode|words}}, {{mode|words}}, {{mode|words}} and {{high|words}}.

$if.then: Three appears three times. {{low|Words}} and {{high|words}} each appear once. The mode is the repeated value three.
$if.else: {{mode|Words}} appears three times. {{low|Words}} and {{high|words}} each appear once. The mode is {{mode|words}}, not three.

scene.description: The three cards with value {{mode|words}} are selected.

constraints.message: Keep the repeated value between the other two values.
Keep the repeated value between the other two values.

lessons.title: Find the range
lessons.label: Find the range
lessons.objective: Find spread by subtracting the minimum from the maximum.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Subtracting in the wrong order or reporting the maximum alone.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do the other three values not affect this range?

steps.title: Read the data
steps.explanation: Range measures how far the data stretches, from its smallest to its largest value.

steps.title: Find the largest value
steps.explanation: {{max|Words}} is the largest value. Keep the minimum in view too.

scene.description: The minimum {{min|words}} and maximum {{max|words}} are selected.

steps.title: Subtract minimum from maximum
steps.explanation: The range is {{answer|words}}. We measure the gap, not the number of values in the set.

scene.description: Subtract the minimum {{min|words}} from the maximum {{max|words}}.

constraints.message: Keep the data ranks strictly ordered.

lessons.title: Read a bar chart
lessons.label: Read a bar chart
lessons.objective: Read a labelled category against an equally spaced frequency axis.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Reading the width of a bar or counting grid lines instead of axis values.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: What does each step on the vertical axis represent?

steps.title: Read the category labels
steps.explanation: This chart records favourite-pet votes. The vertical axis counts votes in steps of one.

scene.description: Cats received {{cats|words}} vote{{cats|s}}, dogs {{dogs|words}} and fish {{fish|words}}. The vertical axis runs from zero to six.

steps.title: Choose the dogs category
steps.explanation: Find Dogs along the bottom, then follow its bar upwards.

scene.description: The Dogs label and bar are selected.

steps.title: Read across to the numbered axis
steps.explanation: The top of the dogs bar lines up with {{dogs|words}} on the votes axis.

scene.description: A dashed guide connects the top of the dogs bar to {{dogs|words}} on the vertical axis.

steps.title: State the reading
steps.explanation: {{dogs|Words}} people voted for dogs. Bar height shows frequency; bar width does not.
